title: Locale realia
description: The things a joke or a sentence is ABOUT, in one language, which a stage draws or measures: what the Cat hears instead of a pig, the things that begin with the sisters' letter, the measure Alice's height is given in. Text layer: keyed by stable ids, it may name a thing but never a scene, shot, beat or demo. Required for every locale in full, like ui.json, and ids are added only when a stage needs one. A demo declares the ids it reads (realia in its demo file); the build writes this locale's entries for just those ids onto the page. See docs/text-experience-binding.md, Language differences.

$schema.description: Optional editor hint; not part of the data.

locale.description: Must equal the directory name, so a copied file cannot silently claim another language.

cat-mishearing.description: The thing the Cheshire Cat hears instead of a pig: the word in this language's text that rhymes with or nearly sounds like its word for pig.

picture.description: A figure id in the art registry, or a figure name the stage that draws it knows.

m-things.description: The things the Dormouse's sisters drew, all beginning with this language's letter, in the order the sentence lists them.

picture.description: A figure id in the art registry, or a figure name the stage that draws it knows.

height.description: The measure this language's text gives Alice's height in. Its label is UI copy (demoHeightUnit); numbers are formatted with the locale profile's numbers tag.

unit.description: A stable name for the unit, for tests and the page; never shown.

perInch.description: How many of this unit make one inch.

notch.description: The height, in this unit, the text names as hers: the reading a stage marks with a notch (three inches; one finger).

marks.description: The marks this language's readers write for yes and for no, as the jury writes them on their slates (important, unimportant): a tick and a cross, or a circle and a cross where a tick reads as wrong. Shapes a stage draws, never letters.

yes.description: The shape for yes: a tick, a circle, or a cross.

no.description: The shape for no: a tick, a circle, or a cross.
